text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A leftist prisoner is murdered by her inmates after far-leftist illegal organisation orders executions of two sisters in separate jails. The surviving one is under strict security of the state.
- Islamist-led government prepares a new law on the Turkish flag which is expected to be effective before Republic Day celebrations on Oct 29.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan realises his project of hosting a summit held between the major countries of the Islamic world in Istanbul.
- Bloodthirsty locals queue up to see macabre house where 10 people were massacred in an "honour killing" in Istanbul at the weekend.
- Police forces are criticised for allowing extreme religious groups fulfil their weird ceremonies and insult Kemal Ataturk, founder of secularist modern Turkey.
- Deputy from the conservative wing of the government is fired from her party for voting in favour of an opposition-led censure motion against the ruling coalition.
- Europe applauds Turkish quality as Turkish tyre maker company Brisa wins the European Quality Award in Edinburgh.
- Atas refinery halts production after it finds a seven percent rise in petroleum prices unsatisfactory.
- The inflation rate has doubled due to the seven percent price rise to petroleum products.
